thread:
dinesh: Heads-up — saw a nasty regression on staging: large-seqlen runs (8k+) show periodic HBM bandwidth spikes and massive KV-cache evictions. Perfetto + nsys traces attached.

alice: Any change in batching heuristics recently?

ben: I ran a quick perfetto capture: https://perfetto.dev/trace?url=redwood/staging/trace-1796129 (linked) — the timeline shows repeated memcpy peaks on cudaMemcpyAsync at ~120ms intervals.

carla: From the logs I'd guess kernel selection fallback is happening for long sequences, we might be switching to the generic GEMM kernel which thrashes the KV pages. I see messages like `selected_kernel=matmul_generic` around the same time.

dinesh: perf-bot also alerted: HBM bandwidth 820 GB/s sustained bursts (threshold 700GB/s) on p4d. Perfetto shows concurrent device-to-device copies + kernel launches.

perf-bot: Automated alert: quota.hbm_bandwidth > 700GB/s (window=1s). Trace: s3://redwood/traces/1796129999/nsys.nsys

alice: Quick theory: eviction waves are probably caused by interleaved microbatches refilling KV cache while other requests still iterate longer seqs. If refills are synchronous we get big memcpy spikes.

ben: I pulled the nsys summary. Relevant lines: 
```
CUDA memcpy HtoD:  1.2s (20%), peak 420GB/s
CUDA memcpy DtoD:  0.8s (13%), peak 390GB/s
Kernel matmul_generic:  total 2.1s, avg concurrency 3
```

carla: That matmul_generic avg concurrency of 3 explains higher memory pressure — kernel uses a different tiling that reads more contiguous KV pages. For long seqs the KV footprint grows and eviction policy starts scavenging pages aggressively.

dinesh: Reproduced locally with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt -o /tmp/run` + PERF counters. The alloc map looks like: many small KV allocations then big ephemeral memcpy spikes.

alice: Could we try 2 quick mitigations: 1) soften eviction aggressiveness (evict_threshold 0.8 -> 0.92), 2) throttle KV refills by staggering async refill across microbatches?

ben: I experimented with staggering: adding a randomized 2-6ms jitter to KV refill start dramatically flattened the peaks in perfetto. Peak bandwidth dropped ~35%.

carla: Also think we should update kernel selection policy: prefer small-seq kernels for any batch item with seqlen < 2048 to avoid generic kernel fallback. That reduces working set per kernel.

dinesh: Agreed. Actionable plan:
- dinesh: add telemetry counters: `kv_evictions_per_sec`, `hbm_bandwidth_peak_1s` (I'll file a tiny PR)
- alice: canary eviction threshold bump on staging and run the perfetto capture again (assign to @alice)
- ben: integrate jittered refill into runtime and run AB test with long-seq workload (assign to @ben)
- carla: draft kernel-selection tweak and perf comparison (assign to @carla)

alice: I'll push the eviction threshold patch in a branch `eviction-soften/1796` and run 3 perfetto captures (baseline, threshold=0.9, threshold=0.92).

ben: One more note — nvprof counters show dram_read_transactions rising when the eviction storm hits. Adding a small LRU hysteresis (do not evict under 15ms since last touch) might reduce oscillation.

carla: We should also add an alert that correlates `kv_evictions_per_sec` + `hbm_bandwidth_peak_1s` before paging to infra oncall. Right now infra sees only bandwidth.

dinesh: Good call. Prioritize tests in staging today. If the jitter + threshold combo reduces peaks we'll roll to dedicated pools.

alice: running first capture now. posting link when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ben: FYI I dumped a small flamegraph for memcpy hotspots and uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/paths/1796129/memcpy-flame.svg — shows memcpy kernels dominate top-of-stack during spikes.

carla: If we cannot fully eliminate thrash, fallback is to limit max-seq per GPU for mixed workloads (route >6k seqlen to dedicated pool). That's coarse but buys stability.

dinesh: Ok. If staging results are encouraging we'll schedule a short maintenance window to roll the eviction threshold change and the jitter. I'll update this thread with capture links.

alice: Capture done: https://perfetto.dev/trace?url=redwood/staging/trace-1796130 — preliminary looks good: bandwidth peaks reduced ~30% with threshold=0.92

ben: Nice. I'll merge jitter experiment to a canary build and run overnight AB tests.

carla: I'll prepare the kernel-selection patch and add unit perf tests for seqlen buckets.

dinesh: Thanks all. Labeling follow-ups in Asana and assigning owners. If anyone finds contradicting traces post-merge ping here. :thumbsup:
